interface.title: Add a CAN interface
interface.description: Pick the CAN interface to add. Interfaces that are already added are not listed.

can.title: CAN interface {port}
can.description: Driver: {driver}. Every node on the bus must use the same bitrate. New interfaces start in listen-only mode.

data_description.listen_only: Never acknowledge or send: watch an existing bus without touching it. Turn it off to send, and on a bus where the only other node needs this host's acknowledgement.
data_description.restart_ms: 0 = stay in bus-off until the entry is reloaded.
data_description.filters: Only receive these IDs, comma separated: 123 (11-bit), 18FF50E5 (29-bit), 7E0/7F0 (ID/mask). Empty = everything.
data_description.event_filter: Received frames with these IDs fire woow_can_frame events and the event entity: 123, 18FF50E5, 7E0/7F0, 100-1FF, * = all. Empty = none (the panel's monitor still shows everything). Each event is written to the history database.
data_description.max_events_per_sec: Events beyond this rate are counted but not fired.

virtual.title: Create a virtual interface
virtual.description: A CAN interface without hardware (vcan), for trying the panel, automations and agents. Frames sent on it by any program on this host are seen by all others. It is re-created after the host restarts and deleted with the entry.

data_description.port: vcan followed by a number, e.g. vcan0.

error.bad_filter: Invalid filter. Use hex IDs, optionally ID/MASK, separated by commas.
error.bad_event_filter: Invalid ID list. Use hex IDs, ID/MASK, FROM-TO ranges or *, separated by commas.
error.bad_vcan_name: Use vcan followed by a number, e.g. vcan0.
error.vcan_failed: Could not create the virtual interface (the host kernel needs the vcan module).

abort.no_interfaces: No free CAN interface found. To try WOOW CAN without hardware, add a virtual interface.

test_signal.description: Read a bit field from the recent frames of one ID (from the interface's buffer): minimum, maximum, number of changes and the last samples, to find where a value sits. Call it with return_response: true.

start.name: Start bit
start.description: DBC numbering: Intel = least significant bit, Motorola = most significant bit.

bit_activity.name: Bit activity
bit_activity.description: Which bits of one ID change and how often, over its recent frames: bits that change on every frame are counters or checksums, bits that never change are unused or fixed. Call it with return_response: true.

interface.name: Interface

can_id.description: Hex: 1-3 digits for 11-bit IDs, more for 29-bit IDs.

limit.name: Frames
limit.description: At most this many of the newest frames.

find_signal.name: Find signal by value
find_signal.description: Find the field that holds a value a person reads off a display or meter, like a memory scanner: start with the value now shown (or without one, then say how it moved), let the value change, narrow with the new value, repeat until one or a few fields are left. Tries bytes, words, nibbles and bits in both byte orders, signed and unsigned, with the usual scalings (0.1, 0.01, 0.5 ..., offsets -40, -273 ...). Start with a value that is not 0. Call it with return_response: true.

interface.name: Interface
interface.description: Name (CAN0), interface (can0) or config entry id.

action.name: Action
action.description: start (a new search, with value or without), narrow (keep what fits mode / value), clear, status.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: For narrow: equals (needs value), increased, decreased, changed or unchanged since the last step.

value.name: Value
value.description: The value shown now, in its unit (52.3 for 52.3 V).

tolerance.name: Tolerance
tolerance.description: How far off the reading may be; default 1 % of the value, at least 0.05.

limit.name: Candidates shown
limit.description: How many of the likeliest fields to return.

guided_capture.name: Guided capture
guided_capture.description: Find what one action changes on the bus. start: the person leaves the equipment idle; next: the person does the action (open the door, press the button, switch the light on) and keeps it so; optionally next again: the person undoes it; finish: the IDs ranked by what differs: bits steady in both phases with another value (a switch), bits that only move during the action, bytes that change level, IDs only sent during the action. Give each phase a few seconds. Call it with return_response: true.

limit.name: IDs shown

add_signal.name: Add signal
add_signal.description: Put a field found with find_signal, guided_capture or test_signal into a device: an existing one (device) or a new one (device_name); the message for the ID is created when the device has none. 1-bit fields become binary sensors, others sensors. Admin only.
